relations.note: Hidesato and Sadamori’s coalition defeated Masakado’s forces in 940.
Hidesato feigned service, learned how to distinguish the true Masakado, and exposed him.
Later romance makes Hidesato shoot Masakado’s vulnerable temple after identifying him among six doubles.

relations.myth: Destruction of the dragon household’s centipede enemy
relations.note: The Dragon King recruited Hidesato to destroy the giant centipede threatening his aquatic household.
The Dragon King rewarded Hidesato with inexhaustible provisions, arms, armor, and a bronze bell.

relations.myth: Dragon woman’s petition against the centipede
relations.note: After testing Hidesato on the bridge, she petitioned him to kill her household’s enemy.
She entertained Hidesato and presented or mediated inexhaustible treasures after his victory.

relations.myth: Later Otohime retellings of the dragon-woman episode
relations.note: Edo and modern retellings name the dragon woman who petitions and rewards Hidesato as Otohime.

relations.myth: Prayer before the decisive centipede arrow
relations.note: Hidesato invoked Hachiman before firing the arrow that killed the giant centipede.
Hidesato fired three arrows against the iron-bodied monster threatening the dragon household.
His saliva-wetted third arrow pierced the centipede between the eyes and through its throat.
Hidesato donated the legendary Dragon Palace bell that Benkei later dragged to Mount Hiei.
